evidence.quote:
You'll be out there on alien worlds where no human being has ever
set foot--worlds which may or may not have been inhabited by hostile
alien creatures.
evidence.paraphrase: The setting establishes human exploration of previously untouched alien worlds.

evidence.quote:
Which was how I happened to be crouching behind a
fantastically-sculptured spiralling rock out on the yellow wind-blasted
desert of Pollux V
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator is located on a distant alien planet, Pollux V.

evidence.quote:
The thing was at least sixty feet tall and all eyes and mouth.
The mouth yawned, showing yellow daggers a foot long.
evidence.paraphrase: A giant alien monster confronts the crew.

evidence.quote:
My hands were trembling--me, who had stood up to Venusian mudworms
without a whimper, who had fought the giant fleas of Rigel IX. I was
shaking all over.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator is shaken with fear despite past combat experience.

evidence.quote:
Max must have
died of fright.
evidence.paraphrase: A crew member is thought to have died purely from fear of the creature.

evidence.quote:
There were _one hundred_ of them, ranging in size from a hunk of rock
the size of Mars' Deimos to one massive high-albedo satellite almost
a thousand miles in diameter.
evidence.paraphrase: The planet has a hundred moons of varying sizes.

evidence.quote:
For one thing, I've been checking
footprints in the sand. I've counted six tracks--one each for you,
Feld, Hamner, Laurence, Forster, and Mickens. Unfortunately, that
doesn't leave any for your monster.
evidence.paraphrase: Donaldson uses footprint evidence to argue the monster left no physical trace.

evidence.quote:
How could that be?" Donaldson asked. "Matter doesn't work that way;
it's flatly impossible.
evidence.paraphrase: A character questions whether the instantaneous appearance is physically possible.

evidence.quote:
I reasoned it out very carefully. Every time Donaldson had gone out
previously, the monster had failed to show.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reasons from the pattern that the monster only appears when Donaldson is present.

evidence.quote:
It's a thought projector.
That monster never existed outside your own mind, Donaldson.
evidence.paraphrase: The device is revealed to be a thought projector that makes imagined monsters seem real.

evidence.quote:
That first day, he had stumbled over an alien treasure in the cave
beyond the hill--that, and the thought-converter.
evidence.paraphrase: Donaldson found an alien thought-converter device that produced the illusions.

evidence.quote:
I sank to the floor, numb with horror--and then realized that the
monster wasn't approaching.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts with horror but then notices the monster is not attacking.

evidence.quote:
Cautiously I touched the monster's writhing surface. It was like
touching a cloud. I sank right in.
evidence.paraphrase: The seemingly solid monster proves immaterial when touched.

evidence.quote:
The monster had taken
a toll of two already, without actually touching either.
evidence.paraphrase: Two crew members die from encounters with the creature without physical contact.

evidence.quote:
So he utilized the thought-converter in a campaign to pick us off
one by one without aiming suspicion at himself.
evidence.paraphrase: Donaldson weaponizes the alien device to murder crewmates covertly.

evidence.quote:
And without a suit, a man was instantly dead on this
methane-ammonia atmosphere world.
evidence.paraphrase: The planet has a lethal methane-ammonia atmosphere requiring suits.
